messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: detected nccl collective hang on gpu-pool-3 (cluster: prod-east). Severity: P1. Symptoms: long all-reduce stalls, repeated CUDA Xid errors on containers tserv-412/413. On-call: @jordan

jordan: I'm on it, joining bridge. seeing repeated `Xid 79` and `cudaDriver` timeouts in the logs. starting triage.

sara: tagging -- this looks like the same pattern as last week where an ephemeral node flapped then containers started OOMing during pipeline allreduce. any node-level telemetry yet?

matt: I have a tail from tserv-412: `ncclCommDestroy` followed by `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` then container restart. pushing main logs to /tmp/nccl-hang-5198765432.log

kai: recommendation: immediately route new TP jobs to single-GPU fallback model variant and reduce pipeline parallel >1 jobs. We can keep a limited capacity for inference by falling back to non-collective path.

jordan: doing routing change now: invoking rollout policy -> fallback-model:tp1 on api-proxy. ETA ~45s. Notifying customers with affected SLA.

infra-bot: Action: cordon node gpu-node-34 from k8s pool (reason: repeated Xid/driver failures). Node marked `unschedulable`.

matt: after cordon, we see existing pods on gpu-node-34 crashed with container runtime error: `containerd: failed to start task: exit status 137` then `driver timeout`. looks like memory corruption or driver mismatch.

kai: while we investigate hardware vs driver, propose rolling-restart of nccl sidecars on remaining nodes to re-establish rendezvous. Command I'll run: ```kubectl rollout restart ds/nccl-sidecar -n serving --timeout=3m```

jordan: matt, run the sidecar restart and watch rendezvous logs. I'll start draining tserv-412 and migrate active jobs.

matt: started sidecar restart. small blip in throughput but rendezvous restored for most shards after ~90s. logs: `rendezvous: handshake complete` on nodes 12/14.

deploy-bot: Container restart completed for tserv-412 (exit 137 -> restarted). Health checks failing on 412 for 30s.

kai: customer-impact: estimated 6% of in-flight requests experienced increased latency or errors during the failover window. affected tenants: acme-ai (heavy TP), beta-recommend. Jordan, can you confirm customer notifications?

jordan: notified SC for acme-ai and posted public status update: "Partial degradation for multi-GPU inference in us-east; fallback routing engaged, mitigation in progress." Link: https://status.redwood.example/summary/5198765432

infra-bot: Hardware team alerted for gpu-node-34 (possible ECC/driver fault). Ticket created: HW-2198.

matt: quick note: found container runtime on node had `nvidia-driver 525.60` but kernel module mismatch on that host. likely reason for illegal address errors.

kai: next immediate actions: 1) keep node cordoned; 2) drain and reprovision with validated driver; 3) keep fallback routing for 2 hours; 4) add an auto-fallback rule to route >90th pct latency to single-gpu variant. I'll open PR for the routing rule.

sara: postmortem items: improve node driver monitoring, add preflight driver check in node-autoscaler, and add a runbook step to trigger single-gpu fallback for TP/PP incidents.

jordan: assigning follow-ups: HW-2198 (infra), SW-7654 (autofallback rule), SW-7655 (runbook update). Will keep channel updated. paging closed for now but will reopen if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Pager cleared at 5198765500. Summary: node driver mismatch caused NCCL hangs -> cordon + sidecar restart + fallback routing mitigated customer impact.
